message.content:
**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales grew 2% to **$391.0B** (FY2023: $383.3B), driven by Services up 13% to $96.2B, while operating income rose 7.8% to **$123.2B** and total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%. Reported net income dipped 3.3% to **$93.7B** and diluted EPS to **$6.08** (from $6.13), but that decline is almost entirely explained by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2B net State Aid income tax charge that pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — operating performance actually improved. Cash generation remains excellent at **$118.3B** of operating cash flow against $9.4B of capex, funding $95.0B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends, with $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Risks noted in the filing (Greater China net sales down 8%, DOJ/EU DMA and antitrust exposure, supply-chain concentration) are real but not thesis-breaking for a modest starter position. I placed a single limit buy order for **44 shares of AAPL at $223.00** — just above the 15:05 UTC quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) so the limit was close to market; it filled at $223.00 for a total of roughly **$9,812**, inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily cap, with no funds leaving the $50,000 cash account and no sales of the existing MSFT position.
